status.label: Check directional-selection policy
status.detail: Current code explicitly tries an eligible zone on the current monitor before moving across monitors; enabled cross-monitor movement does not itself promise a global nearest-zone choice.

next_action.label: Verify same-monitor candidate selection
next_action.reason: Confirm that the reported small zone is a valid same-monitor candidate before treating the policy as a defect or requesting product-direction changes.

judgment.rationale: The reported move to a lower-left zone on the current monitor is consistent with the explicit current-monitor-first relative-position policy. No code defect is established merely by expecting an earlier cross-monitor jump; a maintainer reproduction remains useful to verify candidate eligibility.
evidence: https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/issues/34149 supplies a two-monitor layout, relative-position override and cross-monitor movement enabled, with Windows 11 confirmed in the author reply.
The actual target is a small lower-left zone on the right monitor, whereas the reporter expects a bottom zone on the left monitor.
Current src/modules/fancyzones/FancyZonesLib/WindowKeyboardSnap.cpp explicitly says 'First, try to stay on the same monitor' and returns when that move succeeds.
The bot's suggested 27973 concerns maximization/wrap behavior and closed for missing feedback, not a fix for this case. Related 35510 concerns initially unsnapped windows and index ordering.
judgment.recommended_action: Verify the directional candidate with the supplied layout. If it is eligible, treat globally preferred cross-monitor navigation as a product-policy discussion rather than an already-proven snapping defect.

fix_assessment.rationale: No corrective code fix is currently justified: the stated result matches current-monitor-first selection when a local candidate exists. A different global navigation preference would be a policy change. Reclassify if the local candidate is invalid or cross-monitor movement fails after all local candidates are exhausted.

issue_context.summary: With relative-position snapping and cross-monitor movement enabled, Win+Left selects a lower-left zone on the current monitor instead of immediately moving to the reporter's preferred zone on the adjacent monitor.
known_information: The report identifies 0.83.0, Windows 11, both relevant settings and the starting/actual/expected zone arrangement.
The only human comment adds Windows 11; no maintainer promises the expected navigation policy.
Current navigation explicitly gives same-monitor movement the first attempt.
There are no assignees or linked fix PRs; similarity references are not duplicate proof.
inferences: The smaller zone may be the algorithm's eligible same-monitor leftward candidate.
The exact screenshot geometry must be recreated before concluding that this particular candidate satisfies the direction-selection rules.
issue_context.analysis: The existing source supplies a concrete expected-behavior explanation. Preserve uncertainty about exact geometry and expose a local verification, not a speculative corrective design or an upstream closure comment.
initial_investigation: Read the entire report, bot similarity comment, author reply and complete cross-reference timeline.
Read related 27973 and 35510; their maximization and unsnapped-index cases do not establish a fix for this relative-position case.
Read current WindowKeyboardSnap.cpp's multi-monitor branch: a successful MoveByDirectionAndPosition on the active work area returns before a cross-monitor attempt.
Exact-number PR search found no match. No current-build behavioral test or image-derived coordinate measurement was performed.

information_gaps.information: An exact maintainer reconstruction of the layout to test candidate eligibility and the cross-monitor fallback.
information_gaps.why_needed: Determines whether the example follows the explicit policy or reveals a separate direction/candidate bug.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Maintainer: recreate the public layout, inspect candidate rectangles in the relative-position path, then remove the local leftward candidate and repeat.

reproduce.title: FancyZones relative movement across an asymmetric two-monitor layout
reproduce.version_requirement: Current build; original version was 0.83.0 on Windows 11.
prerequisites: Two monitors arranged left and right.
Recreate the reported layout, including the left column and smaller lower-left zone on the right monitor.
Enable Override Windows Snap, relative-position movement and movement between monitors.
steps: Place a window in the left column of the right monitor and press Win+Left.
Inspect whether the smaller lower-left zone qualifies as a leftward candidate under the current relative-position algorithm.
Repeat with that local candidate removed or moved out of the eligible direction.
Confirm that cross-monitor fallback then works; distinguish candidate eligibility defects from the intentional same-monitor-first policy.
If all behavior matches policy, discuss a different global ranking rule separately rather than silently changing navigation compatibility.
reproduce.expected_result: Eligible same-monitor zones are considered before cross-monitor fallback. A local candidate should not be mistaken for a broken cross-monitor setting.
